newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Chinese groups buy into Australia cotton industry.
newsitem.headline: Chinese groups buy into Australia cotton industry.

text.p: Chinese interests had bought about A$20 million worth of Australian cotton properties in the state of New South Wales during the last 12 months, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Peter Corish, chairman of peak industry body Cotton Australia Ltd, said buyers involved a couple of interests from mainland China as well as one group from Taiwan.
Corish and other industry sources declined to name them.
An official with cotton ginner and marketer, Queensland Cotton Holdings Ltd, said all buyers were involved in domestic cotton activities and some were state-owned.

The groups had bought a total of about 10,000 acres, equal to an annual cotton production of about 30,000 bales, he said. This would not place Chinese interests among the major producers in Australia, compared with Australian interests and other foreign owners, Corish said.
Australian Stock Exchange-listed Colly Cotton Ltd is Australia's largest cotton producer.
It harvested 133,500 bales of cotton in 1996 and expects to harvest 192,000 bales in 1997.
Australia's 1997 cotton crop is currently forecast at 2.4 million 500-pound bales.
U.S. interests would still be the largest foreign owners of Australian cotton properties, led by Auscott Ltd, but owning less than five percent of the Australian growing industry, Corish said.
The Chinese land purchases have been mainly in the Moree area of northwestern New South Wales.
